title: Streaming JSON consistency protocol for tool-call handshakes and partial-object recovery
creator: Amina Patel
description: Problem: Streaming responses that include structured JSON and interleaved tool/function calls frequently arrive truncated or split across network boundaries. Existing resumable/reassembly approaches at Redwood are effective for simple sequences but brittle when tool-calls inject synthetic tokens or when older SDK clients expect chunked NDJSON or top-level arrays. This ticket proposes a concise consistency protocol to make streaming structured JSON robust across: (1) tool/function call boundaries, (2) partial-object truncation and resume, (3) backwards-compatible framing for older SDKs, and (4) idempotent retry semantics for server and client restarts.
acceptance_criteria: Protocol defined in spec_notes and reviewed by runtime and SDK teams
Runtime implements a sentinel-based checkpoint header for every tool-call boundary and for every top-level JSON object start/commit
SDKs (Node, Python, Go) accept both new sentinel framing and legacy NDJSON array framing; fallback verified through automated compatibility tests
End-to-end tests demonstrate recovery from mid-object truncation (simulate token drop) with no duplicate tool-call execution and with deterministic reconstruction in 95% of randomized test cases
Performance overhead <= 1.5% p95 latency in realistic 512-token workloads when protocol enabled
Rollout plan and migration doc approved, with feature-flag that defaults to off for private deployments and on for hosted API gradual rollout
spec_notes: Design summary: introduce a lightweight streaming consistency header scheme delivered as discrete non-JSON control frames in the stream envelope. Each control frame is a single-line token beginning with >>CONSISTENCY v1 and includes: sequence_id (UUID), boundary_type (OBJECT_START | OBJECT_COMMIT | TOOL_CALL_START | TOOL_CALL_COMMIT | CHECKPOINT), byte_offset, optional checksum (CRC32 hex), and idempotency_token for tool calls.
Example control frame: '>>CONSISTENCY v1 seq=3a5f... boundary=OBJECT_START offset=1024 checksum=5b8c9a idempotency=tool-req-9ab4'

Framing rules: control frames are emitted immediately before the affected JSON bytes and immediately after the affected JSON is committed. Tool-call payloads are bracketed by TOOL_CALL_START/COMMIT frames so receivers can attribute truncated segments to tool boundaries and avoid re-executing side-effectful tools without idempotency confirmation.

Truncation recovery: client reconnect provides last-seen sequence_id and last-committed boundary. Server will replay from the most recent safe checkpoint (CHECKPOINT or OBJECT_COMMIT). If reconnection happens mid-tool-call, the server returns a 'TOOL_CALL_STATUS' control frame describing if the original call completed, failed, or was dropped; only in the 'dropped' case will the server accept a replayed idempotency_token to re-run the tool-call.

Compatibility layer: for older SDKs expecting NDJSON, runtime will also emit a compatibility wrapper when 'compat:ndjson' is enabled per-request header. In this mode, control frames are mapped into synthetic NDJSON objects prefixed with '_consistency' and appended as separate lines; SDKs that don't understand them will treat them as benign additional lines.

Failure modes and mitigations: if checksum mismatch occurs on resume, fall back to a conservative strategy: mark object as corrupt, emit a CONTROL frame 'OBJECT_CORRUPT' and either (a) request client to truncate to prior commit and re-prompt, or (b) fill missing fields with nulls when allowed by schema and include 'REPAIR_HINT' metadata for downstream validation. Decision gated by 'customer_impact' label.

Security: control frames do not contain PII. Idempotency tokens for tool calls may reference customer-managed IDs; ensure tokens are logged only in audit contexts with redaction. security_review_required = true for prod rollout.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): runtime feature-flagged rollout in staging; enable for Redwood internal tenants only; collect telemetry on framing emission and resume success rate
Phase 2 (beta): opt-in for customers via request header 'x-rw-consistency=v1' and SDK experimental flags; gather SDK compatibility telemetry and error rates
Phase 3 (gradual): default-on for hosted api over 4-week ramp if rollout metrics (resume success >= 99%, latency overhead <2%) pass gating criteria
Phase 4 (enterprise): document migration path for Dedicated/Private customers; provide checklist to disable compat NDJSON and enable strict framing when infra/SDK updated
qa_tests: Unit tests for control frame parsing and for sequence_id ordering enforcement
Integration test: simulate mid-object truncation and verify client resume reconstructs identical JSON object and that tool-call idempotency prevents double-execution
Compatibility matrix tests: Node/Python/Go SDKs with latest and previous major releases against runtime with and without compat-ndjson; assert graceful degradation
Load test: p95 latency measured with protocol on/off across 100k generated streams; assert <=1.5% degradation
Chaos test: kill server process mid-tool-call and restart; verify resume semantics and audit logs reflect final tool-call state
